newsitem.title: FRANCE: Slide in French earnings forecasts slows in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Slide in French earnings forecasts slows in Nov.

text.p: Consulting firm Associes en Finance said brokers cut French corporate earnings forecasts this month but the decline was much smaller than it had been in the two previous months.
"After two months of sharp reductions, analysts' estimates in November seem more encouraging," Associes en Finance, which surveyed 18 brokerage firms, said in a statement.

Overall, the brokers cut their earnings per share estimates by 1.5 percent in November. The drop was due mainly to big cuts in earnings forecasts for insurer GAN, De Dietrich, shoemaker Andre, and SGE.
"If those firms are excluded, the revision is close to zero," it said.
For the companies listed in the CAC 40 index, the revision was up 0.4 percent, reflecting a rise in Alcatel Alsthom earnings forecasts.
Profit growth in the CAC companies is seen at 29.1 percent in 1996 compared with 1995 levels and at 17.9 percent in 1997.
